title: Iran adds more than $1bn in oil revenue to foreign reserves
summary:
Iran adds more than $1bn in oil revenue to foreign reserves

Iran received more than $1bn in oil revenue during the 11 days to September 2, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Fars said documents reviewed by its reporter showed that authorities had transferred the foreign currency generated by oil exports into Iran’s reserves.

The inflow will strengthen the central bank’s ability to cover the country’s foreign currency requirements, the report added.

Iran generated more than 80 percent of the oil income forecast in its 2026-27 budget during the first five months of the fiscal year, which began on March 21.

title: Israel admits it assassinated senior Assad official in Syria in 2008
summary:
Israel admits it assassinated senior Assad official in Syria in 2008

Submitted by Alex MacDonald on Thu, 09/03/2026 - 10:17
New book says Muhammad Suleiman oversaw construction of nuclear reactor in Deir Ezzor
Muhammad Suleiman was a senior aide to Syrian President Bashar al-Assad (AFP)
Off

Israel has admitted to assassinating a senior aide to former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in 2008, after years of official silence.

In a new book by former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, he admits to the killing of Muhammad Suleiman. 

The Syrian officer was a chief military and intelligence aide who was also in charge of the construction and security of the Syrian nuclear facility in Deir Ezzor.

Though a leaked document from the US National Security Agency in 2015 appeared to confirm that Israeli naval commandos carried out the assassination, Olmert's book is the first high-profile public admission on the subject.

“He [Suleiman] and his guests were sitting on the balcony, and the soldiers approached under the cover of darkness to a distance of 150 meters on either side of the balcony, and confirmed his identity,” wrote Olmert in an excerpt from his book seen by the Ynet news site.

“Even though there were quite a few people on the beach, nobody noticed them.”

He said when the order was given, “three bullets were fired at Suleiman, hitting the back of his head”.

“Immediately afterward, the soldiers retreated to the coast, on the way to the boat that picked them up,” wrote Olmert.

Death of Syrian in police custody sparks protest and conversation about prison reform
Read More »

Assad's government, which was overthrown in December 2024, had long pointed the finger at Israel for the assassination.

A UN report released on Tuesday confirmed that Assad's government had been overseeing construction of a nuclear reactor in Deir Ezzor.

According to the report, inspectors with the UN nuclear watchdog visited several sites in Syria in August to carry out verification work.

In his book, Olmert said Suleiman “had a hand in everything” in the Deir Ezzor facility.

“A month before the attack, he received a new Mercedes from Assad as a token of appreciation for his contribution to building the reactor,” he wrote.

The Deir Ezzor nuclear reactor was also the target of an Israeli strike in September 2007 while Olmert, who would later be imprisoned for six years on bribery charges, was in office.

title: Iran warns US of retaliation if Israel storms southern Lebanon ridge
summary:
Iran warns US of retaliation if Israel storms southern Lebanon ridge

Iran has warned Washington that it will launch a major retaliatory attack if Israel mounts a full-scale offensive on the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, three officials briefed on the message told Reuters.

  • Tehran delivered the warning through Oman in mid-August, according to two regional officials. A third official said US pressure prompted Israel to postpone an assault on the strategically important ridge.

  • More than a dozen members of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including at least two senior officers, are sheltering there alongside Hezbollah fighters, two officials said. Hezbollah neither confirmed nor denied their presence.

  • Israeli forces occupy territory south of Ali al-Taher and have designated the ridge a “primary operational focus”. Israel has attempted to besiege those inside and intercept drones delivering food and water, according to an official familiar with the situation.

  • Hezbollah said it still controlled the hill and would confront any Israeli advance. “Iran considers any Israeli move on the ground in southern Lebanon, especially territorial expansion, a major violation of the Islamabad Agreement,” its media office said, referring to the June US-Iran memorandum that included a Lebanon ceasefire.

  • Israel has continued attacking the area despite the ceasefire.

  • The White House rejected the account of Iran’s warning, saying: “this is not accurate.”

title: Iran says no one can reopen Strait of Hormuz without its consent
summary:
Iran says no one can reopen Strait of Hormuz without its consent

Iran will decide whether vessels can pass through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Ebrahim Azizi, chairman of parliament’s National Security Commission.

Azizi said Iran’s adversaries had withdrawn more than 800km from the region after previously maintaining a military presence there.

He said they had turned to “malicious actions” after failing to “unlock” the strategic waterway.

Azizi added that Iran had delivered “the strongest blows” against the sites it targeted, demonstrating Tehran’s ability to carry out its warnings.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: FBI يعيد إلى لبنان قطعا نادرة كانت مهربة إلى نيويورك

title: إيران تشن هجمات على الكويت، والصين تدعو إلى "هيكل أمني جديد" للشرق الأوسط

title: Iran urges UN action over deadly US attack on wedding
summary:
Iran urges UN action over deadly US attack on wedding

Iran has accused the United States of committing a “war crime” by bombing a wedding gathering in southern Hormozgan province.

In a letter to the United Nations Security Council, Iranian Ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi described the attack on civilians as an “appalling” and “egregious” crime that violated international law.

Darzi urged the UN to “hold the United States fully responsible” and ensure it brings “an end to its acts of aggression” against Iran.

The US strike killed at least four people, including two children, and wounded 50 others at the wedding in Sirik.

Iran’s Health Ministry said recent US air strikes had killed at least 18 people and wounded another 142.

title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
summary:
'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?"

Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. 

"Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president.

"I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed."

It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year.

title: UK must reject attempts to derail an Israeli settlement trade ban
summary:
UK must reject attempts to derail an Israeli settlement trade ban

Submitted by Ben Jamal on Wed, 09/02/2026 - 16:17
If the Burnham government can resist pressure from pro-Israel groups, this could mark the first step in a broader boycott campaign - one long sought by Palestine advocates
British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband is pictured in Wicklow, Ireland, on 2 September 2026 (Paul Faith/AFP)
Off

There are mounting rumours that the UK government is planning to introduce a ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements. 

Such a ban has been a core demand of the Palestine solidarity movement for many years, as a key basic step towards ending UK complicity with Israel’s violations of international law.

That it is now close to achievement is a product of two factors. The first is the increasing untenability of the position adopted by successive UK governments, which have treated Israel as a democratic ally to be shielded from accountability, while sustaining rhetorical support for Palestinian self-determination.  

The hypocrisy of this position, maintained even as Israel’s military occupation and apartheid descended into full-blown genocide, is collapsing under the weight of the increasingly brazen Netanyahu government, whose “Greater Israel” project aims to cement Jewish supremacy and remove any possibility of a Palestinian state.  

As it undertook the genocidal destruction of Gaza, Israel simultaneously accelerated settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, while retroactively legalising settlement outposts, demolishing more Palestinian homes, and facilitating an epidemic of settler violence.  

The government’s plan to lift a two-decade freeze on the building of settlements in the E1 zone - which would effectively cut off the West Bank from East Jerusalem - finally triggered UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to announce a series of “comprehensive” measures in response. 

The second factor is the recognition by incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham that the sustained complicity of his predecessor, Keir Starmer, in Israeli violations of Palestinian rights - even amid a genocide - was a key reason for Labour’s declining public support.  

It is an acknowledgment that winning back voters requires going beyond Burnham’s weak apology for Starmer’s early endorsement of Israel’s genocidal assault on Gaza  and failure to back a ceasefire.

Flawed arguments

The question now is whether Miliband’s statement will ultimately lead to a full ban on all illegal trade with Israeli settlements. This will demand willpower, previously lacking on the part of any UK government, to withstand the pressure coming from the Israeli government and its allies.

Israel has already threatened a punitive response to any trade ban, which could include the expulsion of British diplomats, while the usual cast of pro-Israel groups and individuals in the UK are rolling out familiar arguments in an attempt to prevent any meaningful sanctions. Their core argument rests on the shameful allegation that such a step would constitute a hostile act against British Jews, thus falsely conflating a measure to hold Israel accountable with hatred of the Jewish people.

Other arguments similarly fail to withstand serious scrutiny. One is the suggestion that settler violence, while worthy of condemnation, should be understood as the behaviour of a few fringe extremists.

Half of Britons support banning the trade of goods and services linked to illegal Israeli settlements - a tribute to the strength of the solidarity movement

This ignores both the scale of the current violence - the UN reported in June on a campaign of “systematic abuse” of Palestinians by Israeli settlers - and the fact that attacks are often carried out in the presence of Israeli troops, who fail to intervene.

In one recent shocking case, which captured international attention because it involved a family of Palestinian Americans, Israeli soldiers were filmed praying alongside settlers laying siege to Palestinian homes, where they cut off electricity and water supplies. 

In addition, members of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government actively support these actions by settlers. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who oversees administration of the occupied West Bank, in 2023 notoriously praised a settler pogrom in Huwara, saying the village should be “wiped out”. 

What in any other state would be regarded as extremist and racist positions, are endemic across the political mainstream in Israel. This fact undermines a further argument, notably employed by Labour Friends of Israel, that a settlement trade ban could harm moderate candidates in the forthcoming Israeli election. 

The reality is that the only opposition leaders with a realistic chance of victory, Gadi Eisenkot or Naftali Bennett, are both on record denying the Palestinian right to self-determination. The issue at stake in the election is not whether Israel’s occupation, annexation and settlement expansion will continue, but to what degree. 

Seismic moment

A final argument speaks to the fear that a ban on settlement trade would inevitably morph into a full boycott on all trade with Israel, for two reasons: firstly, the extent to which settlements are heavily intertwined with the broader Israeli economy. Secondly, this argument suggests that removing the taboo on significant material sanctions could fuel further boycotts.

This rests on the fact that the UK government, while actively considering significant action on settlements, remains opposed to a full boycott of Israel - a position motivated by the false narrative that Israel’s oppression of the Palestinian people is only an issue of concern in relation to the territories occupied in 1967. 

Will Burnham liberate Labour's Palestine policy from Starmer's dead hand?
Read More »

The reality, however, is that Israel’s military occupation is just one aspect of a wider system of racist domination and apartheid, which extends across all of historic Palestine, including to Palestinian citizens of Israel. This is why the Palestinian civil society movement has long demanded a full programme of boycott, divestment and sanctions, until the apartheid structure is entirely dismantled.

A ban on settlement trade would thus be a seismic moment. It would also reflect the UK’s minimum responsibility in accordance with the International Court of Justice’s advisory opinion of July 2024, which affirmed the illegality of the Israeli occupation and called for an end to all support by third-party states.

Those who attempt to tie British Jews to a position of support for Israel’s violations of international law, while urging the UK to continue its complicity in the dispossession of Palestinians, are not just displaying a lack of morality. They are also clearly out of kilter with public opinion.

Recent opinion polls show half of Britons support banning the trade of goods and services linked to illegal Israeli settlements - a tribute to the strength of the solidarity movement in advancing the demands of the Palestinian people.

If the British government does indeed resist the counter-pressure being mounted by those lobbying for Israel, and the Rubicon is crossed, the task will then be to sustain pressure until the UK ends all of its complicity with Israeli apartheid. This would require a full implementation of boycott, divestment and sanctions.

title: UAE President and Trump hold phone call over Middle East developments
summary:
UAE President and Trump hold phone call over Middle East developments 

US President Donald Trump and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed regional developments and bilateral cooperation during a phone call, the UAE state news agency WAM reported on Thursday.

The call between the two leaders touched on "ways to further strengthen ties" in support of their "mutual interests".
